architectureDecisions: D1 — Replace the parallel whitelist. In packages/agent-tools/src/deliver-slice.js set const SLICE_TOOLS = Object.freeze(Object.keys(AGENT_TOOLS)); validateDeliverSlice keeps `typeof slice.tool !== "string" || !SLICE_TOOLS.includes(slice.tool)` and the TypeError message becomes `tool must be one of ${SLICE_TOOLS.join("|")}` (codex|kiro|agy|grok|opencode at this baseline). Do not add a second registry, ranking, or probeDeliverCapability runtime. DELIVERED_TRUTH: SLICE_TOOLS is frozen ["codex","kiro","agy"] while AGENT_TOOLS already includes grok and opencode; invalid("tool must be one of codex|kiro|agy") is the executed rejection.

D2 — Headless/edit/resume contract is already AGENT_TOOL_ADAPTER_V1 on grokTool and opencodeTool (read-only). grok buildInvocation uses --prompt-file, --cwd, --permission-mode acceptEdits / --always-approve, --resume/--continue. opencode uses run --format json, --dir, --auto, --session/--continue, positional prompt after --. parseResult returns {claimedSuccess, finalMessage, sessionRef}. Worker does not edit tool-adapters.js. Pin at Worker start: AGENT_TOOLS keys equal SLICE_TOOLS.

D3 — Backend plus QA fixtures. P1: validateDeliverSlice accepts tool "grok"; runDeliverSlice(slice, {tool: defineAgentTool(grokTool, {command: process.execPath, prefixArgs: [fake-grok.mjs]}), env: {FAKE_AGENT_SCENARIO: "FIX_FIRST"}}) returns ACCEPTED with qa.passed. P2: same for opencode + fake-opencode.mjs. These reuse the BB-104 runDeliverSlice + fake-adapter pattern; they do not require Codex/Kiro/agy or a live grok/opencode install.

D4 — Fail-closed before ACCEPTED. N1: validateDeliverSlice({...slice, tool: "not-a-tool"}) throws TypeError matching /codex\|kiro\|agy\|grok\|opencode/ before spawn. N2: runDeliverSlice(grok slice, {command: join(dir, "no-such-grok")}) returns status TOOL_UNAVAILABLE reason NOT_INSTALLED (resolveSliceTool: AGENT_TOOLS[id] exists, resolveExecutable fails, returns null; runBackendFresh then yields NOT_INSTALLED). Subject is runDeliverSlice, not validateDeliverSlice — validateDeliverSlice does not look at binaries. N3: resumeSupervisedTask still throws RecoveryError TOOL_MISMATCH when tool.id !== handle.toolId before reopen/spawn (already delivered); fixture plants a codex handle and resumes with grokTool.

D5 — Tests in packages/agent-tools/test/deliver-tool-parity.test.js titled BB-128 N1/N2/N3 and P1/P2. Also assert Object.keys(AGENT_TOOLS) deepEqual SLICE_TOOLS via validateDeliverSlice accepting each key. Existing deliver-slice.test.js stays the BB-104 contract.

README deliver sentence names grok and opencode. No Blackboard ids. bin USAGE for deliver stays --slice (tool lives in the manifest).
